title: Filet crochet table runner
subtitle: Traditional filled-and-open mesh in fine cotton thread
excerpt: A traditional filet crochet table runner in fine cotton thread: a 25 × 80 cm runner worked in trebles and chain spaces, with a simple border motif in filled squares across each end.
sourceNotes: Traditional filet crochet technique from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776, Chapter XI: Crochet. Filet table covers and runners are among the most extensively documented items in de Dillmont.

glossaryTerms.definition: A style worked in trebles and chain-2 spaces forming a square mesh grid: empty squares are open; filled squares replace the chain-2 with two extra trebles.

content.text: A filet crochet table runner is a 25 × 80 cm piece in size 10 cotton thread: a traditional table covering worked entirely in
filet crochet

, with a repeating geometric border motif of filled squares across each short end. The body of the runner is open mesh. Traditional filet work requires patience and attention to count: blocked flat, it has the look of drawn-thread work or cutwork linen.

items.label: 1.75 mm crochet hook (or as needed for thread)

content.text: Materials
300 m size 10 crochet cotton thread (100% cotton). Approximately two 150 m balls in white or ecru.
Gauge
1 mesh square (1 tr + ch 2 + 1 tr) = 0.7 cm wide in size 10 crochet cotton with a 1.75 mm hook. 10 mesh squares tall = 7 cm. Work a 10 × 10-square swatch to confirm before starting.
Stitches used
Chain (ch)
Slip stitch (sl st)
Treble (tr). UK term; US equivalent is double crochet (dc)
Double treble (dtr). UK term; US equivalent is treble (tr). Used for border lacets.
Pattern
Open mesh square
1 tr, ch 2, skip 2 sts or ch spaces, 1 tr (one open square = 1 mesh unit).
Filled mesh square
1 tr, 2 tr in the previous ch-2 space, 1 tr (one filled square = 4 tr together).
Foundation
Ch 111. (35 mesh units wide requires 35 × 3 ch + 6 for turning chain = 111 ch.)
Row 1
1 tr in 6th ch from hook, *ch 2, skip 2, 1 tr in next ch; repeat from * across (35 open squares). Turn.
Main body (rows 2, 95)

Work all rows as open mesh: ch 5 (counts as tr + ch 2), *1 tr in next tr, ch 2; repeat across, ending 1 tr in top of turning ch (35 open squares per row). Turn. Repeat until the runner body measures approx. 55 cm from the foundation chain.
Border motif (worked over 20 rows at each short end)

Work the first 10 and last 10 rows as a simple repeating diamond motif: on border rows, replace alternating open squares with filled squares on a diagonal grid. Diamond motif (5 squares wide, 5 squares tall): open, open, filled, open, open / open, filled, filled, filled, open / filled, filled, filled, filled, filled / open, filled, filled, filled, open / open, open, filled, open, open. Repeat this 5-wide diamond 7 times across the 35-wide mesh, centred. Work the centre of the runner as plain open mesh between the two border ends.
Finishing

Weave in both ends. Wet-block by submerging in cool water, squeezing out without wringing, and pinning to size on a blocking mat. Traditional filet linen is pinned using a scalloped edge along the treble posts. Leave until completely dry. This can take 12 hours or more for thread-weight cotton.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Reshape and re-pin when needed. Fine cotton thread may be starched very lightly for table use: a thin starch solution adds body and keeps the mesh open between washes.
